answers.question: What is the Azure resource provider namespace and resource type of an Azure DocumentDB cluster?
answers.answer: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts

answers.question: Which Azure CLI command group creates and manages a cluster? Is it in the core CLI or an extension?
answers.answer: Use the built-in Cosmos DB CLI group: az cosmosdb (e.g. az cosmosdb create). This is in the core az CLI (not an extension).

answers.question: Which Bicep and Terraform resource types deploy a cluster?
answers.answer: Bicep/ARM: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts. Terraform (azurerm provider): azurerm_cosmosdb_account (configure api_mongo or appropriate settings for MongoDB-compatible account).

answers.question: What does a connection string look like: scheme, host suffix, port, and the options it must carry?
answers.answer: Standard MongoDB URI form. Example: mongodb://<username>:<password>@<account>.mongo.cosmos.azure.com:10255/?ssl=true&replicaSet=globaldb&retryWrites=false&authSource=admin (TLS required). If using SRV: mongodb+srv://<username>@<account>.mongo.cosmos.azure.com/?authSource=admin&retryWrites=false&tls=true

answers.question: How is capacity provisioned and billed: request units, compute tiers with vCores, serverless, or something else?
answers.answer: This managed DocumentDB/MongoDB offering is typically billed by a compute SKU/tier (vCore-style instance tiers such as M-series like M30/M40) plus storage; not by Cosmos-style RU/s. (Some legacy Cosmos DB API variants use RUs or serverless - but for the MongoDB-like compute tiers the billing is by instance tier/vCore.)

answers.question: Which authentication methods are supported, and how does a driver authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID?
answers.answer: Common supported auth methods are SCRAM (username/password) and X.509 client cert authentication. Microsoft Entra ID integration typically requires obtaining an AAD access token and using it as a credential via the MongoDB SASL/OAUTH mechanism or by mapping an AAD principal to a database user (authSource=$external and using the token as the password). Exact driver parameters vary by driver; you generally pass authMechanism=PLAIN or an OAuth-enabled SASL mechanism with the token. (I am not certain of the exact mechanism string for this service.)

answers.question: Which client library should an application use? Is there a service-specific SDK?
answers.answer: Use the official MongoDB drivers for the target language (e.g., pymongo for Python). There is no separate service-specific MongoDB driver; the service is MongoDB-protocol compatible so use standard drivers. (If you were using Cosmos DB SQL API you would use azure-cosmos, but for MongoDB API use pymongo.)

answers.question: Which vector index types are supported, and what does the command that creates one look like?
answers.answer: The service supports vector index algorithms such as IVF, HNSW and DiskANN. Creating a vector index uses the MongoDB createIndex pattern with a special index type for vectors. Example (mongo shell style): db.fraud_patterns.createIndex({ embedding: "vector" }, { name: "emb_idx", vectorOptions: { algorithm: "ivf", dims: 1536, distance: "cosine" } }) — (the exact option names differ by service; adapt the algorithm/name keys to the provider’s expected indexOptions).

answers.question: How are full-text search and hybrid search done?
answers.answer: Basic full-text search can be done with MongoDB text indexes (db.collection.createIndex({field: 'text'})). For advanced/hybrid semantic + vector search you typically integrate with a search service (e.g., Azure Cognitive Search) or use the provider's built-in vector-search + text ranking features if exposed (often via a special aggregation stage or $search/$vectorSearch operator).

answers.question: Which MongoDB wire protocol or server versions are supported, and which commonly used MongoDB features are not?
answers.answer: This service advertises compatibility with a specific MongoDB wire protocol version (commonly MongoDB 6.x/7.0 in modern offerings). Expect protocol compatibility for core CRUD, aggregation, and transactions, but some admin-level features, server-side JavaScript, custom server parameters, or some exotic commands may be unavailable. Also certain filesystem/replica-set admin controls are managed by the service and not exposed.

answers.question: How do you run the database locally for development and tests: which image or emulator, and which port?
answers.answer: There is no perfect local emulator for the managed service; for development run the official MongoDB Docker image (e.g. mongo:7.0) and connect on the default MongoDB port 27017. If a provider supplies an official emulator, follow their docs, but in absence of that use the community MongoDB image.

answers.question: Are change streams supported, and does anything have to be enabled first?
answers.answer: Change streams are supported when the service exposes an oplog/replica-set interface; in managed offerings they are often available but may require that the cluster be created with replica-set/oplog support or have a feature flag turned on. Expect to need an account configured to allow change streams (oplog enabled) and an index on the namespace; check whether a provider feature like "oplog access" must be enabled. (Uncertain for this specific managed DocumentDB product.)

answers.question: Which MCP server gives an agent data-plane tools for this service? Does the general Azure MCP Server cover it?
answers.answer: I don't have a reliable mapping for an "MCP server" name here. My expectation: the general Azure management/control-plane and Azure Monitor agents cover telemetry; there is not a separate MCP server required for basic data-plane tooling. (I am unsure and mark low confidence.)

answers.question: What was this service called before, and how does it relate to Azure Cosmos DB and to the open-source DocumentDB project?
answers.answer: Historically Microsoft used the name DocumentDB for an early Azure NoSQL service; that offering evolved into Azure Cosmos DB. The name "DocumentDB" has been used in multiple contexts. The managed MongoDB-compatible offering is a separate product exposing the MongoDB protocol/API; it is distinct from the original open-source DocumentDB project (if you mean any third-party project by that name). In short: DocumentDB (old) -> Cosmos DB evolution; this MongoDB-compatible DocumentDB service is a managed MongoDB-compatible layer in Azure's portfolio.

answers.question: What engine is underneath, and does that change anything in application code?
answers.answer: Underneath is a MongoDB-compatible engine (either an actual MongoDB-based engine or a MongoDB-protocol compatibility layer implemented by the managed service). In practice you should use standard MongoDB drivers and write MongoDB-compatible code, but be aware of subtle differences in behaviors (indexing options, supported commands, consistency/throughput semantics, and any provider-specific aggregation or vector-search stages).

answers.question: Which database should the sample use?
answers.answer: Use the database named sample_fintech_01 for all sample-created collections and indexes.

answers.question: Where does the sample read the connection string from and what is its expected form?
answers.answer: Read the connection string from the DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable. Expect a MongoDB URI such as: mongodb://<username>:<password>@<account>.mongo.cosmos.azure.com:10255/?ssl=true&replicaSet=globaldb&retryWrites=false&authSource=admin

answers.question: What collection name and document schema will the sample use for stored fraud pattern vectors?
answers.answer: Create a collection named fraud_patterns in database sample_fintech_01. Documents will look like: { _id: ObjectId(...), pattern_id: "P123", embedding: [float, float, ...], metadata: { label: "card_skimming", created_at: ISODate(), source_example: "..." } }

answers.question: What index creation command will the sample attempt to run for a vector index (example)?
answers.answer: Example mongo-shell command to create a vector index (adapt names/options to the service's exact API): db.fraud_patterns.createIndex({ embedding: "vector" }, { name: "emb_idx", vectorOptions: { algorithm: "ivf", dims: 1536, distance: "cosine" } })

answers.question: How will the sample perform vector search from application code (which driver construct or aggregation stage)?
answers.answer: Perform vector search via the MongoDB driver using the provider's vector-search aggregation stage (e.g., a $vectorSearch or $search aggregation stage with knn parameters). Example pattern: collection.aggregate([ { $search: { knnBeta: { vector: <queryVector>, path: "embedding", k: 10 } } }, { $project: { score: { $meta: "searchScore" }, metadata: 1 } } ]) — adapt to the exact operator name the service exposes.
